beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Anti-Idiocracy argues that truth needs a culture capable of practicing correction.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A fast, confident error can defeat an explanation when the surrounding incentives reward performance.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book proposes voluntary belonging that examines its own loyalties, leaders, and repeated practices.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its provocative name for this social experiment is a metacult.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers are invited to judge whether shared identity can protect inquiry without becoming another authority trap.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The argument separates equal human dignity from authority over a particular consequential decision.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: No person loses rights because another person understands a technical subject better.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Authority, however, should carry limits of domain, evidence, responsibility, and revocation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This distinction challenges both contemptuous meritocracy and the claim that every opinion deserves equal jurisdiction.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book makes that boundary central to the culture it proposes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A metacult deliberately observes the mechanisms through which it produces belonging and status.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The proposed safeguards include criticism, local autonomy, independent memory, and meaningful departure.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The founder’s declared modesty is insufficient if the actual rules still make that founder irreplaceable.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book treats success as a test because money and recognition create new opportunities for capture.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its proposal remains an experiment whose capacity to correct itself must be demonstrated.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Begin with the introduction’s account of why being right is not enough.
